stories.headline: Nvidia is spending $6 billion to build a US rival to DeepSeek
stories.blurb: Nvidia signed a deal with startup Poolside to create an open AI ecosystem in the US that can compete with Chinese models like DeepSeek and American giants like OpenAI. The partnership aims to produce powerful AI models that run on Nvidia chips and aren't controlled by a handful of hyperscalers.
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia is hedging against a world where its biggest customers also become its competitors.
stories.original_headline: Nvidia Is Spending $6 Billion to Build a Powerful U.S. Alternative to Chinese AI

stories.headline: Alibaba's Qwen model reverse-engineered real code in 30 minutes
stories.blurb: A developer gave Qwen 3.8 27B—Alibaba's open-source model—an actual reverse-engineering task that normally takes hours of manual work. The model analyzed unfamiliar code, figured out what it did, and delivered working results in half an hour. It ran locally, no API calls required.
stories.why_it_matters: Open-source models can now handle real engineering grunt work on your laptop.
stories.original_headline: I gave Qwen 3.8 27B a reverse-engineering job and it finished in 30 minutes

stories.headline: This AI agent can now replicate research papers better than Claude or ChatGPT
stories.blurb: Inherent, a British AI lab founded by DeepMind alumni, released Faraday—an AI agent that reads scientific papers and reproduces the experiments. In benchmarks, it outperformed both Anthropic's and OpenAI's agents at replicating published research, which could accelerate how quickly new discoveries get validated and built upon.
stories.why_it_matters: An AI that can independently reproduce experiments could speed up science verification and discovery
stories.original_headline: Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research

stories.headline: DeepMind is building AI agents that play EVE Online and StarCraft II
stories.blurb: Google DeepMind is partnering with game studios to test AI agents in live multiplayer games. The agents learn to play complex strategy games like EVE Online and StarCraft II alongside humans, building on 15 years of research that started with simple Atari games. Early prototypes are already running in real game environments.
stories.why_it_matters: Gaming is where AI learns to handle messy, unpredictable environments with real stakes.
stories.original_headline: From Atari to EVE Online: Building on 15 Years of AI Research in Games

stories.headline: Anthropic eyes $100B IPO that could value it at $2 trillion
stories.blurb: The Claude maker is preparing what would be one of the largest public offerings in tech history, with bankers pitching a valuation that would surpass SpaceX. The five-year-old company has told potential investors it plans to raise $100 billion when it goes public.
stories.why_it_matters: If successful, it would make Anthropic more valuable than any AI company except possibly OpenAI or Google.
stories.original_headline: Anthropic Could Aim to Raise $100 Billion in Blockbuster I.P.O.

stories.headline: Xiaomi built its own phone chip to run AI on-device
stories.blurb: The Chinese phone maker just launched its own mobile processor for flagship devices, breaking years of dependence on Qualcomm and MediaTek. The chip is designed to handle AI tasks locally on the phone instead of sending data to the cloud.
stories.why_it_matters: Another major phone maker is betting its future on custom silicon for on-device AI.
stories.original_headline: Xiaomi Develops Its Own AI Mobile Chip in Challenge to Qualcomm
